title: Text scan over tree-sitter for K8s manifest reference extraction
context: Hunch needed to extract cross-resource references from Kubernetes manifests (ConfigMap/Secret/PVC/owner/Ingress refs), but tree-sitter-yaml's error recovery catastrophically fails on the most common real-world pattern: block-form `{{ include ... }}` injections in metadata.labels and spec.selector, collapsing the entire rest of the document into an unstructured ERROR node.
decision: Implement a line-oriented indentation-tracking text scanner instead of tree-sitter AST walk. Never interprets `{{ }}` as YAML syntax — treats template expressions as opaque strings. Name matching accepts both literal equality and exact raw template-expression text equality (without evaluation).
consequences: Immune to the template-injection error recovery collapse that breaks tree-sitter on production charts
Correctly handles the common case where resource names and references both use identical shared-helper calls like `{{ include "chart.fullname" . }}`
Requires explicit indentation and YAML structure tracking in code (more complex than tree-sitter would be if it worked)
Faster and simpler than complex error recovery fallbacks
alternatives_rejected: tree-sitter CST walk: documented failure on block-form template injections placed early in manifests, poisoning all downstream field-path extraction
